header.running_head: The Enthusiasm of Hadhrat Umar (RA) for Jihaad and His Statement that Jihaad is Better than Hajj

blocks.text: The Enthusiasm of Hadhrat Umar (RA) for Jihaad and His Statement that Jihaad is Better than Hajj

Hadhrat Umar (RA) is reported to have said, "I would have preferred to meet Allaah had it not been for three things; for walking in the path of Allaah, for placing my head on the sand in prostration before Allaah and for sitting in the company of people who choose their words just as the best dates are selected."[^1]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) is also reported to have said (to the people), "Ensure that you perform Hajj for it is a virtuous deed that Allaah has commanded. However, Jihaad is even more virtuous."[^2]
The Enthusiasm of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) for Jihaad

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) once said, "When I was brought before Rasulullaah ﷺ to participate in the Battle of Badr, Rasulullaah ﷺ thought that I was too young and did not accept me. I had never experienced no night like that night. Because Rasulullaah ﷺ did not accept me (to fight in Jihaad), I did not sleep a wink, was overcome with grief and wept incessantly. When I was brought before him the following year and Rasulullaah ﷺ accepted me, I praised Allaah for it." Someone then asked him, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! Did you people turn back on the day the two armies met (during the Battle of Uhud)?" "Yes," replied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), "but Allaah forgave all of us, and all thanks are due to Him."[^3]
The Incident of Hadhrat Umar (RA) With the Person who Intended to Proceed in Jihaad

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and requested, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Please provide me with transport because I want to proceed in Jihaad." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then told someone to take the man to the public treasury so that he could take whatever he required form there. When the man entered the treasury and found gold and silver, he asked, "What is all this? I need none of this. All I require are provisions for a journey and transport." The people took the man back to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and informed him about what he had said. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then issued instructions that the man should be provided with provisions and transport. (When these were brought) Hadhrat Umar (RA) himself tied the saddle to the animal. After mounting the animals, the man raised his hands (in du'aa) and praised Allaah for the treatment he received and for what Hadhrat Umar (RA) had given him.
